answers.reason: ¶3 'it is expected' WFI for parenterals with pyrogen concern, covering both formulation and final washing; recommended, and parenteral scope maps to INJ/API.
The products in ¶4 (ophthalmic irrigating solution, Sterile Water for Inhalation) are sterile products with pyrogen specifications, so the text applies only to INJ/API, not to LIQ, which is listed.

In ¶6 antacids are given only as an example for oral/topical products with marginally effective preservatives. The text does not apply to API, which contains no preservative system, and 'have to be set' is stronger than recommended.
¶6 says QC 'should' assess each product made with the water and base action limits on the most microbially sensitive product. The statement captures this fully.
¶6 says the manufacturer 'can' add a microbial reduction step in lieu of stringent limits, which is optional, and the statement matches.
¶8 quotes PDA guidance that challenging an on-line system is undesirable and that reliance is placed on periodic testing and checkpoint monitoring. The statement matches as a recommendation.
¶9 'Documentation should include a description of the system along with a print'; recommended and complete.
¶9 says the drawing needs to show all equipment from feed to points of use and should show all sampling points and their designations. Both are captured under the 'should be considered' lead-in.
¶9 says the print 'should' be compared to the system annually for the three listed purposes. The statement includes the frequency and all three purposes.
¶10 says the initial phase begins after equipment and piping are verified and develops operating parameters and cleaning/sanitization procedures and frequencies. The statement captures both.
¶10 says sampling 'should' be daily after each purification step and at each point of use for two to four weeks. The statement keeps all qualifiers.
¶10 says point-of-use sampling 'should' reflect how the water is drawn, giving the hose and flush examples. The statement is complete.
¶10 says the firm 'should' have developed its operating SOPs by the end of the two to four weeks. The statement matches.
¶11 describes the second phase: same sampling and period, with data that 'should' demonstrate consistent quality under the SOPs. The statement is complete.
¶12 describes the third phase: long-term operation under SOPs, routine sampling, and picking up feedwater variations. The statement captures it as a recommendation.
¶12 says WFI samples 'should' be taken daily from at least one point of use, with all points tested weekly. WFI scope maps to INJ/API.
¶12 says validation is completed when the firm has a full year's data, and the statement matches.
¶13 'there must be data to support the SOPs'; mandatory as worded.
¶13 says there must be data showing the SOPs are valid and that the system consistently meets specifications. Mandatory, and the statement is complete.
¶13 says there must be data showing that seasonal feedwater variations do not adversely affect operation or water quality. Mandatory, and the statement is complete.
¶14 says the data and conclusions are compiled into the final report, and the statement matches as a recommendation.
¶14 says the final report 'must be signed' by the people responsible for operation and QA. Mandatory, and the statement matches.
¶15 gives the solution as procedures that open the secondary valve before the primary to flush the drained pipe. The statement matches and includes the purpose.
¶16 says consistent results throughout the system over time are the primary element of the acceptance criteria. The statement matches.
¶17 says WFI results are 'expected' to be essentially sterile, which is recommended. WFI maps to INJ/API.
¶17 says less than 10 CFU/100 mL is an 'acceptable' action limit for WFI, which is optional, and the statement matches.
¶17 says none of the water limits are pass/fail and all are action limits. The statement matches.
¶17 says the firm 'must' investigate, correct, assess the product impact and document when action limits are exceeded. All elements and the condition are included.
¶18 says 100-300 mL is preferred and less than 100 mL is unacceptable for WFI sampling. Both parts are captured.
¶19 says it is important to monitor WFI systems for both endotoxins and microorganisms, which is recommended, and the statement matches.
¶20 recognizes the USP specification of compliance with EPA drinking water regulations as the minimal specification for purified water. The statement matches as a recommendation.
¶20 says any purified water action limit over 100 CFU/mL is unacceptable. The statement (no more than 100 CFU/mL) matches.
¶21 says the action limit depends on the overall system, the further processing of the finished product and its use. The statement is complete.
¶21 says purified water for cold-processed drug products 'should' be free of objectionable organisms. The condition is included.
¶23 says setting contamination levels for water used for non-sterile products requires understanding the product's use, formulation and process. INJ is correctly excluded.
¶23 says products like antacids that lack an effective preservative system require an action limit below 100 CFU/mL. This applies to the non-sterile dosage forms listed.
¶24 sits in the non-sterile product context (USP Non-Sterile Products monograph, the 100 CFU/mL maximum from ¶23), so it does not apply to INJ, which is listed.

¶26 says pretreatment is 'definitely required' for RO units, which is mandatory, but only recommended by still manufacturers for distillation. The item merges both under 'recommended', so the strength does not match for RO.
¶27 says a water system 'should' be designed to operate within the anticipated feedwater extremes described in ¶26. The statement matches.
¶27 says the only way to know the extremes is to periodically monitor feedwater, and the statement matches.
¶27 says municipal reports 'can' be used in lieu of in-house testing, which is optional, and the condition is included.
¶30 says that without a satisfactory pretreatment system it is extremely difficult to demonstrate validation, which implies it is expected. The statement matches.

¶31 tells the investigator to examine design, changes, the validation report and routine data for a state of control when WFI still problems are seen. The firm is expected to be able to show this, and the condition is included.
¶33 says sampling ports between equipment are necessary to isolate major equipment for qualification and investigations. The statement is complete.
¶34 says positive pressure (vapor compression or double tubesheet) 'should be employed' to prevent feedwater-to-distillate leakage contamination. The statement matches.
¶35 gives the two methods (differential pressure gauges with the clean side higher, or a double tubesheet). The statement captures both as alternatives.
¶36 says it is recommended that use-point heat exchangers not be drained of cooling water when not in use. The statement matches.
¶38 says it is expected that there be a program for integrity testing the vent filter. Recommended, and the statement matches.
¶39 says it is expected that the vent filter be readily accessible on the holding tank. Recommended, and the statement matches.
